overview.label: Overview
overview.body_html:
Flake8 is a code style checker that runs automatically when you submit to CodeGrade. It checks your Python code against PEP 8: the official Python style guide used by professional developers worldwide.

These aren’t just suggestions. They’re part of your Code Style grade. Clean code is professional code. See the Rubrics section on Grading Info for how Code Style factors into your overall lab grade.

anatomy.desc: Which file the error is in

errors.title: Module Imported But Unused
errors.intro_html: You imported something but never used it. Remove the import!
errors.problem_html:
import math
# math is never used!
print("Hello")
errors.fix_html:
# Removed unused import
print("Hello")

errors.title: Variable Assigned But Never Used
errors.intro_html: You created a variable but never did anything with it.
errors.problem_html:
result = 5 + 3
# result is never printed or used!

rows.fix: Put 2 blank lines before every function definition
Never have more than 2 consecutive blank lines
Keep lines under 79 characters; break long strings across multiple lines
Remove invisible spaces at the end of lines (VS Code can do this automatically)
Use exactly 4 spaces per level, never mix tabs and spaces

breakingLongLines.label: Breaking Long Lines
breakingLongLines.subtitle_html: E501 is the style error you will hit most. Flake8 flags it when a line runs past 79 characters. Here are the go-to ways to break one up, roughly in order of how often they are the right answer.

techniques.title: Split a long string across lines
techniques.intro_html: Python glues adjacent string literals together automatically, so you can just break the text.
techniques.code_html:
print("This is a very long message that goes way beyond "
      "the 79 character limit")

techniques.title: Pull part of it into a variable
techniques.intro_html: Often the cleanest fix, and it usually makes the line easier to read too.
techniques.code_html:
message = "This is a very long message"
print(message)

techniques.title: Backslash continuation for long calculations
techniques.intro_html: A trailing backslash tells Python the statement continues on the next line.
techniques.code_html:
total = first_value + second_value + third_value + \
        fourth_value + fifth_value

techniques.title: Use the parentheses you already have
techniques.intro_html: If the line is a function call, break after any comma inside the parentheses. No backslash needed.

techniques.title: Long if conditions
techniques.intro_html: Wrap the whole condition in parentheses, then break at the and or or.
techniques.code_html:
if (miles_remaining > 0 and
        fuel_level > 10):
    print("Keep driving!")

techniques.title: Long f-strings
techniques.intro_html: Compute the value first, then keep the f-string itself short.
techniques.code_html:
trip_summary = f"{miles_driven} of {total_miles} miles"
print(f"Progress: {trip_summary}")

quickFixes.label: Quick Fixes
quickFixes.intro_html: Run through this list before every submission:
items_html: 2 blank lines before each function definition
4 spaces for each indentation level (not tabs)
No trailing whitespace at the end of lines
All variables you created are actually used
All imports at the top are actually needed
